entries.reason: no controller is attached on this release, so the snapshot is the zeroed structure; the encode is the measured one and the two sizes come from the header layout, 4 + 8 + 6 floats = 36
entries.effect: reads the gamepad's dpad and its six buttons into a GCGamepadSnapShotDataV100 and answers a GCGamepadSnapshot holding the encoded 36 bytes; with no controller attached every value is zero and the data is 0001 2400, which is the encoding measured in facts/GameController/Snapshots.md
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4

entries.reason: owed, and not for want of the work: the SDK declares -saveSnapshot at 7.0 (GCExtendedGamepad.h:65) returning GCExtendedGamepadSnapshot, which first appears at 9.0. One object per release forbids the 7.0 file to name the 9.0 class: the method's IMP emits an objc-class-ref for it, and the 6.1.3 band has no 9.0 object to satisfy it, so the dylib does not link. Measured: with the method built, GCSnapshots7.o carries an undefined _OBJC_CLASS_$_GCExtendedGamepadSnapshot; without it the object names only GCGamepad, NSData, NSDictionary and NSNumber, all of which 6.1.3 has. A forward @class declares without emitting; the method's return type does emit. Queued in coordination/api-queue.md
entries.effect: until that collision is resolved the method is not declared, so respondsToSelector: answers honestly and an unchecked call raises, rather than a 7.0 object handing back a class it cannot build
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4
